diagnostic_evidence.quote: We shall show that with the step size in \eqref{thetastar}, the KM iteration converges faster to the fixed point than the standard fixed-point iteration.
From the above theorem, we know that the convergence speed increases as the momentum parameter $\theta$ approaches $\theta^*$ in each iteration.
Of course, the expression for $\theta^*$ involves $\hx$, the desired solution, which is naturally unknown.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the paper proves that the KM iteration with momentum converges faster than Picard iteration. Theorem thm_KMaccel only compares a single step taken from the same point x: ||T^theta x - xhat|| < ||Tx - xhat||. Moreover, theta* depends on the unknown fixed point xhat. After one step the KM and Picard trajectories sit at different points. A bound ||x^k - xhat|| <= ||y^k - xhat|| does not propagate, because ||Tx^k - xhat|| need not be <= ||Ty^k - xhat||. Hence no trajectory, rate, or complexity comparison follows. Nothing comparable is proved for the computable surrogate theta_k used in TKMA. Its proven rate o(1/sqrt(k)) is the same rate that Lemma generalconvergerate (with c_k = 1) gives for plain Picard iteration of an averaged operator.

failure_location.quote: We rigorously prove that KM momentum accelerates convergence for averaged nonexpansive operators with appropriate momentum parameters.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the contribution as a one-step distance-reduction property along the momentum direction, using the oracle theta*. Alternatively, supply a genuine trajectory-level or rate comparison argument.
issues.overall_effect: Contribution (ii) and the motivating claim that the momentum accelerates convergence are unsupported. Only a per-step distance reduction with an oracle parameter is established.
issues.title: Acceleration by KM momentum is claimed, but only a one-step comparison using an unknown fixed point is proved
issues.why_classification: No formal result changes, but the honest correction withdraws an advertised contribution (proved acceleration). Restoring it would need a new argument that the source lacks.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the parameters $\mu$ and $\lambda$ are set to $10$ and $0.999/4$, respectively
It is easy to see that this operator is averaged nonexpansive when $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$
The step size parameter $\alpha$ is set to $1.99$.
thereby ensuring the convergence rate of TKMA as established by the theorem

issues.failure_explanation: All TKMA results (prop:thetarange(ii), lem:monotonic, thm:conv, convergerate) need alpha in (0,1/2]. For alpha > 1/2, alpha(1+theta_k) can reach 2*alpha > 1, so T^{theta_k} need not be nonexpansive and the proofs break. For the applications the paper only shows that T_2 and T_3 are averaged, with no constant <= 1/2. In fact T_3 is not 1/2-averaged at step 1.99. Here grad f(X) = P_Omega(X - A) and L = 1. On the nonempty open set where X - 1.99 grad f(X) lies in int C, T_3 is affine with linear part I - 1.99 P_Omega, which has eigenvalue -0.99. Lemma lem:equivAN with alpha = 1/2 requires e^2 + (1-e)^2 <= 1, i.e. e in [0,1], so this fails. T_2 behaves the same way. Where A(y) lies inside the l_inf ball on which I - prox_{phi/lambda} is the identity, T_2 is affine with linear part I - lambda B B^T. That map has negative eigenvalues once lambda*||B||^2 > 1, as with lambda = 0.999/4. Despite this, the paper asserts that the theorem's rate guarantee holds in the denoising experiment.

failure_location.quote: Thus operator $T_2$ defined by \eqref{operatorTfordenoising} is averaged nonexpansive when $\lambda<\frac{1}{4}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply TKMA to the 1/2-averaged relaxation S = (1 - 1/(2alpha))I + (1/(2alpha))T, which has Fix(S) = Fix(T), with alpha taken from a composition bound, and rerun the experiments. Alternatively, explicitly restrict the theoretical claims to alpha <= 1/2 and state that the reported experiments lie outside them.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence and o(1/sqrt(k)) guarantees are not established for TKMA as run in the denoising and matrix-completion experiments. The claim that the theory underpins these applications is unsupported.
issues.title: The convergence and rate theory (alpha <= 1/2) does not cover the operators used in the experiments
issues.why_classification: The theorems themselves stay valid. Restoring coverage of the applications needs a contained change (operator rescaling plus re-running the experiments) or a scope restriction, not new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we present in Figure \ref{sumthetak} the plots $\sum_{k=0}^{n} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|$ for TKMA against its iteration count $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis of convergerate concerns the infinite tail of the sequence |theta_{k+1} - theta_k|. Any finite set of partial sums is consistent with divergence; for example, increments of order 1/k give partial sums that grow only logarithmically and look flat on a finite plot. The o(.) conclusion is also purely asymptotic. A finite run therefore cannot verify the condition or ensure the rate.

failure_location.quote: This experimentally verifies that the condition $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|<+\infty$ in Theorem \ref{convergerate} is satisfied in the denoising scenario

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the claim as numerical evidence consistent with the summability condition, not as a verification that ensures the rate.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the convergence rate is guaranteed in the denoising experiment is unsupported. The figure is only heuristic evidence.
issues.title: A finite plot is claimed to verify an infinite summability hypothesis and to ensure the asymptotic rate
issues.why_classification: Rewording this one sentence suffices. No theorem, method or rate claim of the paper is lost.
